statement: The fix is cited as f211fe9f, which does not resolve in the public repository babyblueviper1/invinoveritas; a3527263, cited for the relay widening in the same comment, does. The fix may live in a repository that is not public (the chain_note names ledger_forward_verdict.py, which is not in the public tree). The effect is checked against the served data separately and is not in question here; only the citation is.

The fix is dated 2026-09-21, but every one of the six entries carries chain_backfilled_at on 2026-09-30 (2026-09-30T12:58:49+00:00 to 2026-09-30T12:58:59+00:00), and their chain_note says 'chained late (2026-09-30)'. The served data is self-consistent; the date in the description is not what the ledger says. On the served dates the backfill landed roughly three quarters of an hour before this project's first fetch of the ledger, which matches 'found while preparing the earlier snapshot for you'.

Signed heads were found on 5 of 9 relays queried (7 reachable), and they cover 15 of 239 chained entries (264-278); 224 chained entries have no signed head on any relay queried. A head is the only anchor that catches a consistently rewritten chain, so a reader who holds no head for the range they care about has nothing to hold the chain to. The relay set itself is wider than it was: the gap the operator raised as fixed in a3527263 is measured here, not assumed.

20 valid signed head events on public relays -- same ledger key, same schema invinoveritas.ledger_chain_head.v1, same d-tag family -- claim entries 1-20, which the served ledger does not chain: chain_spec says the chain starts at entry 40 and GET /ledger carries chain blocks only from there. The head for entry 1 gives prev_head_hash as the published genesis constant, so on the relays alone those events read as a second chain rooted at the same genesis. They do not affect the grade below -- the chain 40-278 recomputes and matches the head for 278 -- but a verifier that picks 'the newest signed head under this key and schema' can pick from the wrong series, which is the ambiguity the 264-269 incident was about, moved from the chain into the head namespace. Pinning the d tag, or putting a chain identifier in the signed content, would close it.
